     and where the edges are. Keep it under two screens. -->

## What the system does
The platform turns a natural-language goal into working Mistral AI building blocks: agents, Python tools, workflow activities and multi-step workflows. It is presented to clients as the "TCS Dynamic Agentic Workflow Composer".

A business user describes what they need. Layered planning pipelines then:
- design the agent or workflow, one focused model decision per layer;
- write and sandbox-test any missing code in a separate Tool Service;
- check it against the organisation's rules, process knowledge and credentials;
- register it with Mistral (agents, libraries, connectors, Mistral Workflows), or run it locally on a DAG engine.

The outcome is a saved, versioned and runnable agent or workflow. A person can inspect it, refine it with AI, approve its human-review steps, deploy it to a remote server and monitor it.

## Users and roles
| Role | What they do in the system | How they get access |
|---|---|---|
| Platform admin | Manages workspaces (one Mistral API key each), users, roles, other admins, Settings writes, the vault master key and cleanup. Sees the audit log, health and cross-workspace logs. Does not build or run anything. | Created at first start from `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD`, or invited by another admin. Signs in at `/admin/login`. Stored in `auth_admins`, separate from users. |
| Maintainer (built-in role) | Has every workspace permission (all 26), including `vault.reveal` and `workflows.deploy`. | Granted per workspace by an admin, through a membership. |
| Builder (built-in role) | Has every `.view` permission, plus orchestrator.use, chat.use, agents/tools/connectors/knowledge/vault manage, workflows.run and workflows.manage. Cannot deploy, reveal secrets or decide reviews. | As above. |
| Operator (built-in role) | Has every `.view` permission, plus chat.use and workflows.run. | As above. |
| Reviewer (built-in role) | Has every `.view` permission, plus reviews.decide (approve, edit or reject human-review steps). | As above. |
| Viewer (built-in role) | Read-only: every `.view` permission. | As above. |
| Custom role | Any subset of the 26 permissions. | Created by an admin at `/admin/roles`. |

Users sign in at `/login`. They are invited (`/invite/$token`) or given admin-issued reset links (`/reset-password/$token`); there is no self-registration and no self-service password reset. A user can belong to several workspaces with a different role in each, and switches the active workspace from the account menu.

## Main capabilities
- **Orchestrator (`/`):** describe a need in chat; a background run designs, tests and creates a Mistral agent.
- **Agent Studio (`/agents`):** list, chat with and configure agents (model, instructions, tools, connectors, libraries, guardrails, rules, domains).
- **AI workflow planner (`/workflows/new/ai`):** goal to validated, saved and registered workflow through the layered workflow pipeline, with user decisions and countdowns.
- **Visual workflow builder (`/workflows/new/visual`, `/edit`):** graph editor with validation, argument wiring and a generated-script preview.
- **Workflow execution:** run forms with document inputs, a prerequisite check, live progress, human reviews, results, Mistral execution traces, cancel, terminate and reset.
- **Refine with AI:** revisions, diffs, versions, undo and restore; opened from a failed run to fix it.
- **Tool and activity synthesis:** the Tool Service writes code, tests it in a sandbox and registers versions; pending tools need approval.
- **Connectors and MCP servers:** Mistral connectors (directory and custom MCP) and locally registered MCP servers.
- **Document libraries and graph RAG:** Mistral libraries, entity extraction into Neo4j, per-library ontologies, the query optimiser and timelines.
- **Catalog (ontology):** controlled vocabulary of industries, domains, archetypes and tiers; annotations and classification.
- **Process knowledge:** industry → domain → process tree; process documents and templates used when planning.
- **Knowledge:** build guidance and reference knowledge, distilled from sources and retrieved by condition.
- **Rules and tool-safety rules:** checks agents and workflows must pass, at creation time and at run time.
- **Vault:** encrypted credentials with versions, audit and build-prerequisite resolution.
- **Remote servers:** SSH, Brev and cloud targets; deploy workflows and tools; consoles and diagnostics.
- **Observability and logs:** action traces, workflow traces and rule verdicts; user-facing health page.
- **Playground (`/playground`):** chat with any model, with up to five attachments.
- **Admin console (`/admin/*`):** workspaces, users, roles, admins, audit, health and logs.

## Scope and non-goals
- **Not a general chat product.** Chat exists for testing agents and models.
- **Self-registration, self-service password reset and email delivery do not exist.** Links are issued by admins and copied by hand.
- **No billing or quotas** beyond per-workspace admission slots for background runs.
- **The Tool Service has no authentication.** It is meant to be reachable only on the internal network.
- **The legacy `frontend/` SPA is superseded** and not deployed.
- **Present but partial or mock:**
  - the built-in `send_email` tool is a mock that reports success;
  - the `calculate` tool uses `eval`;
  - `tool-service/app/prompts.py` is dead code;
  - `app/ontology/*` and `app/process_knowledge/*` are legacy import aliases.
- **`unimplemented_mistral_features.md`** at the root lists Mistral features that were deliberately not built.
- **Present but dormant:** `mistral-small-2603` (`LIGHT` in `llm_routes.py`) is defined and used by no route.

## Components at a glance
| Component | Folder | Language / framework | Runs as |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend API | `backend/app` | Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy (SQLite), `mistralai` ≥ 2.6 | `uvicorn app.main:app` on port 8000 (Docker image `python:3.12-slim`) |
| Mistral Workflows worker | `backend/app/services/mistral_worker.py` and the compiled `mistral_workflows/` | Python, Mistral Workflows (Temporal) SDK | A subprocess supervised by the backend, one worker per workspace |
| Tool Service | `tool-service/app` | Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite | `uvicorn` on port 9000 (Docker image `python:3.11-slim`) |
| Frontend | `frontend-3` | TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start/Router/Query, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, zustand | Vite dev server on 8080; in production a Nitro Node server on 3000 |
| Graph store | `docker-compose.yml`, `deploy/docker-compose.yml` | Neo4j 5 community | Container on ports 7474 and 7687 (optional) |
| Reverse proxy | `deploy/Caddyfile` | Caddy 2 | Container on 80 and 443 (production only) |
| Client presentation | `client_explainer/` | Python generators producing HTML | Static files; not part of the runtime |

## Which code is live
- **Live:**
  - `backend/app`;
  - `tool-service/app`;
  - `frontend-3/`;
  - `deploy/`;
  - `mistral_workflows/`, which is generated by the backend;
  - `test_assets/`.
- **History or reference only:**
  - `frontend/`, the old Vite SPA (`npm run dev:legacy`);
  - root Markdown documents such as `README.md`, `architecture.md`, `analysis.md`, `implementation_plan.md`, `hybrid_architecture_implementation.md`, `api_documentation.md` and `LOVABLE_FRONTEND_SPEC.md`. They describe earlier designs; the README still describes the legacy frontend on port 5173;
  - `openapi.yaml`, a stale export;
  - `mock_tools/`, `scratch_tools.json` and `generate_report.py`;
  - the developer scratch scripts at `backend/*.py`.
- **Generated, not hand-written:**
  - `frontend-3/src/routeTree.gen.ts`;
  - `mistral_workflows/*.py`;
  - the HTML in `client_explainer/`.
- **Not source:** `sql_app.db` at the root is a stray local database.
